entries.update: Hillary Clinton was deposed by the Republican-led House Oversight Committee on February 26 as part of an Epstein investigation, with Bill Clinton scheduled for deposition on February 27.

Hillary Clinton and Bill Clinton testified in closed-door sessions before the House Oversight Committee as part of its Epstein investigation, with Hillary Clinton stating she did not know Jeffrey Epstein and Bill Clinton testifying the day after. Neither has been accused of crimes related to Epstein.
The House Oversight Committee released video depositions of Bill and Hillary Clinton on Monday as part of its Jeffrey Epstein investigation. The depositions took place the week before their release.
The House Oversight Committee voted on a bipartisan basis to subpoena Attorney General Pam Bondi regarding the DOJ's handling of Jeffrey Epstein-related files.
The House Oversight Committee voted on a bipartisan basis to subpoena Attorney General Pam Bondi regarding the DOJ's handling of Jeffrey Epstein-related files.
The DOJ released previously withheld documents from the Epstein files, including FBI interview reports relating to allegations made against President Donald Trump by a woman.

Rep. James Comer and the House Oversight Committee are investigating the Epstein case. The federal government requested that New Mexico stop its investigation into Epstein's Zorro Ranch around 2019 during Trump's first term.
Richard Kahn, Jeffrey Epstein's accountant, testified before the House Oversight Committee; Epstein accumulated hundreds of millions of dollars over his career.

Tova Noel, a former prison guard at the Metropolitan Correctional Center who was on duty the night Jeffrey Epstein died, is scheduled to testify before the House Oversight Committee as part of an ongoing congressional investigation.

New documents are revealing Jeffrey Epstein's network of connections and relationships cultivated among powerful and elite circles in the original sex-trafficking investigation that originated in Florida.
Leon Black and his wife Debra purchased the property at 1111 Calle Vista Drive in Beverly Hills for $38 million in 2016, which was subsequently sold for $47 million.

Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche dismissed suggestions that victims of convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein have been ignored by the Justice Department and defended the Trump administration's handling of the investigation.
Metropolitan Police chief Mark Rowley stated police are investigating whether an email from Mandelson to Epstein constitutes a criminal offence.

Democrats walked out of a House Oversight Committee briefing with Attorney General Pam Bondi regarding Epstein files; GOP Chairman James Comer characterized the walkout as premeditated, and Bondi stated she would 'follow the law' in response.
Wall Street titan Leon Black paid Jeffrey Epstein $170 million, which Black described as compensation for tax and estate work.
Leon Black paid Jeffrey Epstein $170 million, which Black described as payment for tax and estate work.
David A. Ross sought Jeffrey Epstein's help to build art museums and is now facing fallout related to that association.
Jeffrey Epstein's accountant Richard Khan and lawyer Darren Indyke testified before the House Oversight Committee, both stating the DOJ never interviewed them about Epstein's crimes.
Epstein survivors filed a class action lawsuit against the Trump administration and Google seeking at least $1,000 per survivor and court-ordered removal of their personal information by Google.
A man was interviewed on suspicion of sex trafficking in connection with the Al Fayed investigation, following earlier interviews with three women under caution.
Ramsey Elkholy introduced Jeffrey Epstein to women as young as 18 years old over nearly a decade, with correspondence documented in emails between them.
Jeffrey Epstein provided funding to scientists, and the lack of legal or public scrutiny in science philanthropy allowed him to cultivate relationships with scientists.
Epstein files indicate a 15-year-old girl met then-Prince Andrew at Buckingham Palace. Mandelson attempted to get access to 10 Downing Street for Epstein's goddaughter.
Attorney General Pam Bondi was fired by President Trump on Thursday; her handling of Epstein files was a point of congressional interest.
The Epstein files were released containing accusations against rich and powerful people, but the DOJ made no additional arrests, with legal experts citing lack of evidence.
Todd Blanche assumed the role of Interim Attorney General on Thursday, replacing Pam Bondi, and stated he wants to distance the Department of Justice from its work on Epstein files.

Virginia Giuffre, prior to her death, accused Jeffrey Epstein of trafficking her to Prince Andrew, brother of King Charles. The Giuffre family is urging King Charles to meet with Epstein survivors in the United States.
Jeffrey Epstein spent his final days of freedom in Paris, where he met with influential figures.
According to an FBI interview, Epstein had sex in a vehicle in a prison parking lot while on work release from a Florida jail approximately 20 years ago.

Bill Gates has agreed to appear before the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform in June as part of its investigation into deceased sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is also scheduled to testify before the same House panel as part of the Epstein probe.

Attorney General Pam Bondi did not appear for a House Oversight Committee deposition subpoenaed in connection with its investigation into the Jeffrey Epstein files. The DOJ communicated that Bondi would not appear and informed the committee that its subpoena is essentially moot, though committee members maintain the subpoena remains valid.

The Department of Justice announced that Attorney General Pam Bondi would not testify before the House Oversight Committee, at least temporarily, despite having been subpoenaed as part of the committee's probe into the Jeffrey Epstein files. Separately, UK politician Peter Mandelson was reported to have attempted to obtain access to 10 Downing Street for a person described as Epstein's 'goddaughter.'

Melania Trump delivered a televised statement from the White House denying any connection to Jeffrey Epstein, stating 'I have never had any knowledge of Epstein's abuse of his victims,' 'I was never involved in any capacity,' 'I've never been friends with Epstein,' and 'I am not Epstein's victim.' She called on Congress to continue the investigation and hold hearings focused on Epstein's survivors, and declared that claims linking her to Epstein 'need to end today.'

On April 9, 2026, Melania Trump issued a rare public statement denying that Jeffrey Epstein introduced her to Donald Trump and calling on Congress to hold a hearing for Epstein survivors. Former Justice Department chief Pam Bondi refused to appear before a congressional Epstein hearing, with a subpoena for her testimony remaining in effect and Democrats criticizing her absence. Rep. Thomas Massie argued that bringing survivors back before Congress would be redundant and that the duty to act rests with federal prosecutors.

Melania Trump issued a rare public statement on Thursday denying any ties to Jeffrey Epstein, calling him 'disgraceful.' The statement was described as unexpected given her typically low public profile, and her adviser spoke publicly about what motivated her to issue it.

Melania Trump made a surprise public statement calling for testimony from Jeffrey Epstein victims. House Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer, a Republican from Kentucky, responded to her statement and confirmed that congressional hearings featuring Epstein victims will take place. Separately, Epstein survivors pushed back on the call for public testimony. The House Oversight Committee has been investigating allegations of sex trafficking connected to Epstein, who was a convicted sex offender and is deceased.

A federal judge dismissed Donald Trump's defamation lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal, which had centered on the outlet's reporting about a letter allegedly connected to Jeffrey Epstein's 50th birthday. The judge ruled that Trump failed to sufficiently allege 'actual malice,' the legal standard required for public figures in defamation cases.

The Justice Department's Office of Inspector General announced a review of the DOJ's compliance with laws requiring the release of Epstein-related records, amid concerns that required documents have not been fully disclosed.

Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick appeared before the House Oversight Committee on Wednesday in connection with the Epstein investigation. Ahead of the hearing, Committee Chair James Comer told reporters that Lutnick was not '100% truthful' about visiting Epstein's island.

A federal judge ordered the release of a document purported to be a suicide note attributed to Jeffrey Epstein, with the unsealing occurring on a Wednesday following a request by The New York Times. The note's authenticity has not been fully verified. Lutnick's testimony before the House Oversight Committee was conducted as a closed-door session.

Former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene claimed on CBS News that President Trump is targeting Republicans who voted to release Epstein files, citing Rep. Thomas Massie's primary defeat as an example. Separately, a trespasser who illegally accessed Epstein's private island Little St. James claimed he was hog-tied and held in a dungeon on the property.

British police issued a public appeal for witnesses on a Friday as part of an investigation into potential sexual misconduct offenses by former Prince Andrew, with the probe connected to Jeffrey Epstein. Newly released papers revealed Prince Andrew was coached on how to justify his qualifications for a UK trade ambassador role after lawmakers accused him of prioritizing his Epstein ties over British interests. Sarah Kellen, described as both an alleged survivor and recruiter for Epstein, testified in a closed-door session before lawmakers, reportedly naming three individuals tied to abuse. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick donated $5 million to House Republicans after agreeing to be interviewed by lawmakers about his relationship with Epstein, according to the New York Times.

FEC filings confirmed that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick donated the $5 million to the Congressional Leadership Fund, a House Republican super PAC, on April 1, specifically ahead of his congressional testimony regarding his ties to Jeffrey Epstein.

A U.S. document repository described as a 'library' has been established in New York to house 3.5 million pages of Epstein-related documents, aimed at providing accountability for victims, according to Al Jazeera. Rep. Thomas Massie attributed his primary loss to Trump-backed challenger Ed Gallrein to his bipartisan advocacy, particularly his push to release the Epstein files.

Rep. Thomas Massie, despite losing his primary race after being targeted by President Trump, promised to expose additional names from the Epstein files before his term ends in approximately seven months.

Pam Bondi appeared before the House Oversight Committee in a closed-door transcribed interview on Friday regarding the Epstein files, despite having been removed from her role as attorney general in April. A lawyer representing Epstein survivors told BBC News that his clients lack confidence in how UK police would treat them, casting doubt on their willingness to cooperate with the British inquiry into Prince Andrew.

During her closed-door testimony before the House Oversight Committee, Bondi refused to answer questions about President Trump's involvement in the Epstein files release and instead blamed Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche and FBI Director Kash Patel for issues with the release. Following the interview, House Democrats announced plans to seek subpoenas for both Blanche and Patel. Epstein survivor Danielle Besnky spoke out during the proceedings, stating she wants 'baseline humanity' from Bondi.

New Mexico lawmakers announced they will issue subpoenas to government and private institutions as the first major step in their state investigation into Jeffrey Epstein's activities in New Mexico, with the goal of determining whether additional prosecutions are warranted.
Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche and Rep. Madeleine Dean had a heated exchange during a House Appropriations Committee hearing over the state of the Jeffrey Epstein investigation.

The US and Iran are holding nuclear talks in Geneva aimed at resolving their nuclear dispute, with President Trump accompanying diplomatic efforts with military threats and a Middle East force buildup.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated progress has been made in negotiations with Iran after the U.S. sent a draft peace proposal to Tehran.
Following US-Israeli attacks on key infrastructure, Iranian hardliners and politicians are demanding withdrawal from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty.
Iranian President Pezeshkian released a letter to Americans on X hours before Trump's scheduled address on Iran operations.
Iran rejected a U.S. ceasefire deal and instead conveyed a 10-point counterproposal through Pakistani intermediaries. The proposal demanded an end to ongoing attacks and an end to sanctions.

Pakistan has been mediating backchannel talks between the United States and Iran, with U.S. Vice President JD Vance involved in the mediation efforts. Iran has sought indirect engagement through the U.S. vice president.
Iran's ambassador to Pakistan stated that an Iranian delegation is scheduled to arrive in Islamabad on Thursday.
Negotiations between the U.S. and Iran are being hosted in Islamabad as both sides seek a diplomatic off-ramp to the conflict.

High-stakes U.S.-Iran negotiations were set for Islamabad this weekend, with Vice President JD Vance leading the American delegation in talks aimed at ending the war and finalizing ceasefire terms. The White House described the talks as ongoing, while Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei stated through state TV that Iran does not want war and seeks compensation. Some Republicans in Congress moved to assert legislative authority over any lasting deal with Tehran, citing a 2015 Obama-era law. China's role in the negotiations was also under discussion, with NBC News correspondent Janis Mackey Frayer covering that dimension of the diplomacy.

Vice President JD Vance traveled to Islamabad, Pakistan, to lead U.S. talks with Iranian officials aimed at ending the ongoing conflict, stating he expects 'positive' negotiations and that President Trump provided 'pretty clear guidelines' for the discussions. Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad-Bagher Ghalibaf posted on X that Iran will not negotiate with the U.S. without a ceasefire in Lebanon and the release of blocked Iranian assets, adding that two mutually agreed-upon measures have yet to be implemented. A fragile ceasefire remains in place, though multiple hurdles continue to strain it.

US and Iranian delegations convened in Islamabad, Pakistan, for high-stakes nuclear and diplomatic talks, with Pakistan serving as host and mediator. Vice President JD Vance participated on the US side, and a US plane carrying the American team was confirmed to have landed in Islamabad by two Pakistani sources. A fragile ceasefire between the US and Iran is currently in place, with the Strait of Hormuz among the key issues under negotiation.

Vice President JD Vance traveled to Islamabad, Pakistan on Saturday for direct talks with Iranian officials, the first such direct U.S.-Iran negotiations since 1979. The White House confirmed the talks, with Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif playing a mediating role in hosting the negotiations. A two-week ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran, described as fragile, remains in effect, and Iran is seeking sanctions relief as part of the discussions. Special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner participated in trilateral talks with Iranian officials, drawing criticism from Sen. Mark Kelly. The Strait of Hormuz remains a key factor in the negotiations. Separately, Saudi Arabia confirmed that Pakistan sent fighter jets to the kingdom under a mutual defense pact.
After approximately 21 hours of negotiations in Pakistan, Vice President JD Vance announced that no deal was reached between the U.S. and Iran, describing the outcome as 'bad news for Iran.'

Trump initially told CNBC he did not want to extend the ceasefire with Iran, but ultimately announced an extension before the deadline expired. The extension is conditional, remaining in effect until Iran submits a proposal and discussions are concluded, while the blockade against Iran stays in place.

Iran submitted a response to a U.S. peace proposal aimed at ending the war, according to Iranian state media outlet IRNA. No details of Iran's response or the contents of the U.S. proposal have been publicly disclosed.

Trump claimed in a Fox News interview with Sean Hannity that during his talks with Xi Jinping in Beijing, Xi offered to help with Iran, specifically related to keeping the Strait of Hormuz open. Trump also stated that Xi committed to not providing military equipment to Iran, describing the pledge as significant.

Trump stated that the United States will retrieve uranium from Iran, reflecting tensions over its enrichment activities. Iranian Supreme Leader Khamenei has ordered that enriched uranium remain inside Iran rather than be transferred elsewhere. The U.S. Senate advanced a bill aimed at ending the war with Iran, with Senator Cassidy switching his position to support the measure after losing a primary election.

Trump announced via Truth Social on Saturday that a deal with Iran is 'largely negotiated,' stating that 'Final aspects and details of the Deal are currently being discussed, and will be announced shortly,' following a phone call with Gulf and regional Arab leaders to review Iran's latest proposal. The proposed deal would include reopening the Strait of Hormuz and formally ending the war between the U.S. and Iran. Secretary of State Marco Rubio separately stated that 'significant progress' has been made in negotiations. However, Iran and Iranian state media dismissed Trump's characterization as inconsistent with reality, and a senior Iranian source told Reuters that Iran has not agreed to hand over its highly enriched uranium stockpile, contradicting U.S. officials cited by the NY Times who said Iran had agreed to relinquish enriched uranium. Republican war hawks urged Trump to abandon peace efforts, and Senator Lindsey Graham raised concerns about the potential agreement, while details of what has formally been agreed upon remain unclear.
The White House dismissed an outline of an 'unofficial' Iran deal, according to the NY Times.

Wall Street investors are broadly assuming a U.S.-Iran nuclear deal would be a net positive for stocks and risky assets, though analysts also raise the possibility it could trigger a market selloff. Separately, analysts suggest oil prices may not return to previous lower levels even after the conflict concludes.

Trump announced he is convening advisers in the White House Situation Room to make a 'final determination' on a deal with Iran, posting the announcement via social media. Trump also demanded that Arab and Muslim countries normalize relations with Israel through the Abraham Accords as a condition for ending the conflict, a last-minute linkage that U.S. allies pushed back against, according to NBC News. Former national security adviser John Bolton publicly called the tentative deal 'a big defeat for the United States' and a 'mistake,' alleging it is driven by Trump's concerns over high gas prices ahead of midterm elections.

Iranian state media announced the suspension of all peace talks with the United States following U.S. and Israeli strikes. Trump described the negotiations as 'very boring' and told CNBC he 'couldn't care less' if they break down. IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi stated that the 2015 JCPOA is no longer a workable model and that any future nuclear agreement with Iran will look significantly different.
Russia launched drone and missile strikes on Ukrainian cities and infrastructure near the time of scheduled US-Ukraine talks in Geneva.
A Russian-operated gas tanker sank in the Mediterranean Sea following a Ukrainian drone attack, which Russia attributed to Ukraine.
A Russian-flagged gas tanker sank in the Mediterranean Sea following a drone attack that Russia attributed to Ukraine.
Russian publication Izvestia reported that Ukraine peace talks have been paused in connection with the Iran war.
Ukraine reported hitting a Russian oil terminal at Primorsk and a refinery in Ufa on Monday.
Zelenskyy stated that Ukraine has evidence that Russia is supplying Iran with intelligence.
Russia launched a large drone attack on Ukrainian cities including Lviv, damaging a UNESCO World Heritage site and injuring multiple people.
Ukrainian President Zelenskiy stated that the US has linked security guarantees to Ukraine ceding Donbas territory.
Ukrainian President Zelenskiy stated that the US has linked security guarantees to Ukraine giving up Donbas, according to Reuters.
Zelensky visited Saudi Arabia and offered Ukraine's drone expertise.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky made a surprise visit to Saudi Arabia to offer Ukraine's drone defense expertise developed during the war against Russia to the U.S. and Gulf States.
Russia announced a ban on gasoline exports starting April 1.
Russian strikes on Ukraine killed 4 people, and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio expressed openness to diverting weapons to Kyiv.
Ukrainian drones damaged Russia's Ust-Luga port, causing a fire to break out.
President Zelenskyy stated in an NBC News interview that he hopes President Trump cares about Ukraine's future, noting that Trump administration priorities center on the United States.
Ukraine's president stated that allies asked him about reducing attacks on Russian energy as prices rise due to the Iran war.
Estonia's defence forces detected an air threat overnight.
Ukraine's president hosted EU leaders at an event marking the Bucha massacre anniversary while Ukraine's negotiator Umerov was in Turkey for talks.
A Russian military transport plane crashed in Crimea, killing 29 people, according to the Russian Defense Ministry.
A Russian military transport plane crashed in Crimea, killing 29 people. Officials cited possible technical malfunction.
Russia is recruiting students for its drone forces in Ukraine and offering large financial packages as part of recruitment efforts.
Ukrainian President Zelensky warned about Russia's intelligence sharing with Iran in an exclusive NewsNation interview and discussed Ukraine's assistance to the US in its conflict with Iran.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned in an exclusive interview about Russia's intelligence sharing with Iran and discussed how Ukraine is helping the US in its war against Iran.
Fuel leaks occurred at Russia's Primorsk oil facility and a fire broke out at the NORSI oil refinery in Nizhny Novgorod, according to Russian authorities.
Zelenskiy traveled to Syria and met with President Sharaa.
A child was rescued from rubble after a Russian strike collapsed a home in Odesa, killing at least three people.
The Iran war has driven shortages and price spikes across multiple consumer product categories beyond oil and gas, including beer cans, helium balloons, and mortgages.

Farmers warned that the Iran war and its associated costs would drive up their expenses and subsequently affect food prices, with the recently announced ceasefire not expected to immediately relieve those pressures.

Vladimir Putin announced a ceasefire coinciding with Orthodox Easter weekend, including April 12, and both Russia and Ukraine signaled agreement to the truce. President Zelensky stated that Ukraine will complete repairs to the Druzhba oil pipeline in spring and said peace talks to end the war could resume soon, though he expressed skepticism about any imminent breakthrough.

A 32-hour Easter truce was established between Ukraine and Russia, though both Ukrainians and Russians expressed doubt it would lead to lasting peace. Russian casualties are mounting, recruitment is falling, and territorial gains are dwindling, while Ukraine has been increasing drone production. President Zelensky traveled to the Middle East in March, securing a series of 10-year agreements with Gulf State leaders, and subsequently announced that Ukrainian interceptors had downed Iranian drones in the region, with 228 Ukrainian experts previously deployed there.

Russian drone strikes killed at least two people in the Ukrainian city of Odesa overnight into Saturday, according to local authorities. A Ukrainian drone attack in Russia's Kursk region injured three people, as reported by the regional governor. Separately, Ukraine and Russia exchanged 175 servicemen each ahead of an Easter ceasefire.
Russia launched one of the most intense aerial attacks of the year on Ukraine, sending hundreds of drones and missiles overnight in a hours-long assault targeting civilian areas across the country.
Vladimir Putin declared his belief that the war with Ukraine is 'coming to an end' as a new three-day ceasefire went into effect.
Ukraine launched one of its largest drone attacks on Russia, killing at least four people, three of them in the Moscow region.

Russia conducted joint military exercises with Belarus that included delivering nuclear warheads to Belarusian sites, with the drills described as rehearsals for the use of nuclear forces. Ukraine conducted attacks targeting Russian energy infrastructure sites as part of ongoing military operations.

Russia condemned a Ukrainian strike on occupied Luhansk as a 'monstrous crime,' claiming a student dormitory was hit and at least four people killed. Ukrainian officials reported Russia has suffered approximately 83,000 soldiers killed so far in 2026 and is actively seeking to recruit new soldiers, with independent estimates also suggesting Russia's economy is faltering.
Putin vowed retaliation following the Luhansk strike, while Ukraine stated the attack targeted Russia's elite Rubicon drone military unit operating in Moscow-occupied eastern Ukraine.

The drone strike on a student dormitory in Russian-controlled Luhansk was reported to have killed 16 people, with most victims described as young women, adding detail to previously reported Russian accusations. Ukraine claimed it struck Russia's Sheskharis oil terminal on the Black Sea. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy warned that Russia is preparing to strike Ukraine using a hypersonic 'Oreshnik' missile.

Russia launched a massive missile and drone attack on Kyiv overnight, killing at least four people and injuring more than 50, including three children, with damage reported at 40 locations across the capital and nearby areas. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy stated the attack included Russia's hypersonic Oreshnik ballistic missile, which Russia confirmed it deployed using hypersonic and ballistic missiles, though the NY Times reported it remained unclear whether the Oreshnik was used. Prior to the attack, Zelenskyy had warned on social media that Ukraine was bracing for a 'significant air attack' involving hypersonic missiles and stated Ukraine was working to verify U.S. and allied intelligence on Russia's Oreshnik deployment plans.

Russia's Oreshnik ballistic missile strike on Ukraine — its third such use since the war began — was confirmed by Ukrainian President Zelenskyy as part of Sunday's barrage on Kyiv, which killed four people and injured approximately 100, with damage reported to 30 residential buildings.

European leaders condemned Russia's hypersonic ballistic missile strike on Kyiv. Energy infrastructure was also damaged in a separate missile attack on Russia's Belgorod region, according to local authorities cited by Reuters.

The EU is actively searching for potential mediators to help broker an end to the war in Ukraine following U.S. withdrawal from trilateral talks, according to BBC News. Ukraine used British-supplied Storm Shadow missiles in an attack on Sevastopol, according to the city's governor. The GCHQ Director is set to deliver a speech Wednesday warning that Russia is 'relentlessly targeting' critical infrastructure and democracy, outlining threats facing the UK and proposed countermeasures. UN Secretary-General Guterres expressed being 'deeply concerned' following Russia's announcement of plans to strike Kyiv.
GCHQ Director Anne Keast-Butler, in her first public speech, stated that almost 500,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the Ukraine war.

Ukrainian President Zelensky appealed directly to Trump and members of Congress on Wednesday, requesting Patriot missile interceptors and citing Ukraine's lack of domestic capability to produce anti-missile defense systems. The U.S. Embassy in Kyiv denied reports of an evacuation, disputing claims by EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas that Washington had withdrawn personnel amid escalating Russian airstrike threats. Ukrainian veterans returning from the front are facing a growing mental health crisis, according to a Washington Examiner report from Lviv.
Russia dismissed a U.S. call not to launch systemic strikes on Kyiv, according to Reuters, signaling continued disagreement between Moscow and Washington over attacks on the Ukrainian capital.

A Russian drone struck an apartment building in Galati, eastern Romania, near the Ukrainian border overnight Friday, injuring two people with minor wounds — the first confirmed Russian drone strike on Romanian territory. Romanian officials confirmed the incident, and Russian officials acknowledged the drone was targeting Ukraine when it drifted off course. Dmitry Medvedev issued a public warning following the incident, declaring that Europe's 'peaceful sleep is over' and asserting that European authorities have 'unilaterally entered into a war with Russia.' Separately, Russia's diesel output fell an additional 10% in May following drone attacks on Russian energy infrastructure, according to Reuters data.
Russian drone strikes on public buses in Kherson have killed three transport workers so far in 2025, according to BBC News, with drivers continuing to operate routes despite the ongoing danger.
Ukrainian President Zelenskyy stated his government has evidence that Russia is abducting thousands of Ukrainian children and forcing them to fight in the war, according to CBS News.

Russia launched a large-scale overnight attack on Ukraine using 656 drones and 73 missiles, according to Ukraine's air force, striking cities including Kyiv and Dnipro. At least 11 people were killed and dozens injured, with residential buildings and civilian infrastructure damaged and people trapped inside collapsed or damaged buildings. Separately, the Washington Post reported that Russia has failed to achieve its war aims in Ukraine and that Putin is seeking a way out of the conflict. Ukrainian startups are also developing sea drone swarms and autonomous robot trucks to bolster the country's defenses, according to Reuters.

Russian overnight strikes across Ukraine killed at least 13 people, with the death toll expected to rise as emergency responders continue searching for survivors trapped in rubble. A Kyiv resident described the attack as feeling like 'some kind of apocalypse.' The NY Times reported Russia has intensified strikes amid recent battlefield losses and mounting casualties, with Moscow seeking to improve its position ahead of potential negotiations.

A drone struck a bus traveling between Moscow and Simferopol in Russian-controlled territory, killing seven people, with Denis Pushilin, the Russian-installed leader of the Donetsk region, confirming the attack. Ukraine launched a large-scale drone attack on Russian targets early Wednesday, with Ukrainian drones striking and setting ablaze an oil terminal in St. Petersburg as the city hosted the St. Petersburg International Economic Forum, an annual economic forum promoted by President Putin. The death toll from recent Russian overnight strikes across Ukraine has risen to at least 22, including children, according to Al Jazeera. BBC News reported that concern over the war is growing even among Putin loyalists more than four years into the conflict.
Ukrainian drones struck an oil or energy facility in St. Petersburg as Vladimir Putin's annual St. Petersburg International Economic Forum was opening, with black smoke visible over the city.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio told a Senate Appropriations subcommittee that the Russia-Ukraine war 'has no military solution' and warned that escalation risk is 'more real than it was two years ago,' citing concerns over increasing long-range exchanges. The U.S. House advanced new sanctions on Russia and aid to Ukraine, with six Republicans and one Independent joining Democrats to force the measure to the floor, bypassing Speaker opposition after GOP leaders had previously blocked the legislation.
Culiacán in northern Sinaloa state is experiencing a significant surge in cartel-linked violence.
El Mencho, a top figure in Mexico's criminal underworld and associated with the Sinaloa Cartel, died.

Trump held the inaugural Shield of the Americas summit in Doral, Florida and announced a new military coalition aimed at eradicating drug cartels in the Western Hemisphere. Kristi Noem was appointed as Special Envoy for the Shield of the Americas after being removed as DHS Secretary.
The US Coast Guard intercepted a semi-submersible vessel in the Pacific Ocean carrying 17,600 pounds of cocaine.
The US military struck an alleged drug trafficking vessel in the Pacific, killing two people and leaving three survivors.
The DEA named a Colombian leader a priority target and prosecutors are probing ties between the Colombian leader and drug traffickers.
An undocumented MS-13 gang member from El Salvador was sentenced to 35 years in prison in Southern California for a murder connected to a 2019 gang arrest.
The Colombian navy shut down 30 drug labs, seized 2 tons of cocaine, and seized thousands of gallons of smuggled fuel.

Érick Valencia Salazar, a co-founder of the Jalisco New Generation drug cartel, was extradited to the United States from Mexico as part of a group of 29 alleged drug lords and subsequently pleaded guilty.

Ten current and former Mexican officials, including Sinaloa state Governor Rubén Rocha Moya, have been charged in a U.S. federal indictment for drug trafficking offenses connected to the Sinaloa Cartel.
Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya has stepped down from his position following the U.S. federal drug trafficking charges filed against him.

U.S. drug czar Sara Carter issued a warning about medetomidine, a veterinary sedative known as a 'rhino tranquilizer,' appearing in the U.S. drug supply mixed with fentanyl and linked to American deaths, amid the administration's escalating cartel crackdown.

Mexican military captured Isai 'N,' nephew of former Sinaloa cartel leader Joaquín 'El Chapo' Guzmán, during a security operation in Nogales, Sonora, near the U.S.-Mexico border. Mexican official Omar Hamid Garcia Harfuch confirmed the arrest and noted the suspect has an extradition order.
Reuters reported on a paper trail linking a U.S. fuel trader to a notorious Mexican cartel, though specific individuals and the cartel involved were not identified in available reporting.

U.S. authorities uncovered a cross-border smuggling tunnel running between San Diego and Tijuana, concealed beneath a fake store on the U.S. side, which was used to transport illegal drugs and weapons. Four people were arrested and charged in connection with the tunnel operation.
Iranian authorities are conducting mass arrests of protesters and reformists following a deadly crackdown on anti-government protests.
The Iranian national women's football team returned to Iran after several players withdrew asylum requests.
Iran executed three individuals arrested in connection with protests, as announced by Iran's judiciary.
Iran executed three men, including Saleh Mohammadi, a young member of Iran's national wrestling team; these were the first executions carried out over January protests in Iran.
A State Department spokesperson called Iran's executions 'barbaric'; the UN and activist groups report Iran's regime is using the death penalty to crush dissent.
Iran's judiciary reported that two men involved in January protests were executed.
Iran has carried out executions by hanging, including of teenagers.
Iran released a Japanese national on bail who had been jailed amid antigovernment protests. The released individual is believed to be Shinnosuke Kawashima, NHK's Tehran bureau chief.

The U.S. and Israel launched joint military operation 'Operation Epic Fury' against Iran, followed by Iranian retaliation with missile strikes against U.S. bases in the Middle East and toward Israel. Explosions were reported across multiple Gulf states, airspace closed in several countries, and Israeli defense systems intercepted Iranian missiles over Haifa.
Anthropic's AI technology was used by the US military in connection with strikes on Iran, creating a significant dispute between the Pentagon and Anthropic over the military's use of the AI system.
NATO defense systems intercepted and destroyed an Iranian missile headed toward Turkey on Wednesday; Turkey confirmed the shootdown.
The Senate voted on a war powers resolution seeking to constrain President Trump's military authority regarding Iran, though the measure faced significant obstacles to becoming law.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney called for de-escalation of the Iran conflict while expressing support for the strikes.
The Senate voted on a war powers resolution seeking to constrain President Trump's military authority regarding Iran, though the measure faced significant obstacles to becoming law.

Israel claims to have killed Iran's top security official Ali Larijani and Basij militia commander Gholamreza Soleimani in airstrikes as part of a U.S.-Israel joint military operation that began on February 28. These targeted killings follow Iran's Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's death earlier in the conflict.
The Iranian national women's football team returned to Iran after several players withdrew asylum requests prior to returning.
Putin told Tehran that Russia stands by Iran, according to Reuters.
Iran conducted strikes near an Israeli nuclear research center.
A missile strike hit an elementary school in Minab, southern Iran on February 28, killing dozens of children including Soheil Monazzah.
Iranian missiles struck Israel, with explosions and smoke observed in Israel.
An Iranian missile attack struck the Israeli city of Arad, with drone footage revealing damage captured days after the strike.
U.S. and Israeli airstrikes struck Tehran and Isfahan early morning, with black smoke rising over both cities.
Former U.S. Secretary of Defense Leon Panetta stated there is no clear end to the war in Iran.
President Trump announced 'major combat operations' against Iran on February 28 involving joint U.S.-Israeli strikes; Israel and Gulf states reported Iranian strikes.
The US sent its first shipment of oil to Greece in four years as European refiners seek alternatives to Middle Eastern crude.
Iran has implemented a strategy to impose economic pain on Gulf states to force them to pressure the United States into restraining its actions.
A majority of Israelis support the war with Iran, though many doubt it will solve long-term security problems and question their prime minister's assurances and motives.

An Iranian attack in Kuwait killed six U.S. service members, with survivors disputing the Pentagon's official account of the incident. Pope Leo XIV used the phrase 'delusion of omnipotence' to describe what is driving the war during a vigil at St. Peter's Basilica, again calling for peace in connection with the conflict.

Army survivors of an Iranian attack on U.S. forces in Kuwait disputed the Pentagon's account of the incident, claiming their unit was unprepared to defend itself. A two-week ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran was in effect, while more than 70 Democrats in Congress called for President Trump's removal over his threats against Iran and handling of military operations there. An anonymous Iranian woman described conditions in Tehran to The Australian, including nightly explosions, celebrations, and widespread fear. President Trump cited European nations' unwillingness to back the U.S. in the Iran conflict as a reason to scale back or abandon NATO commitments.

More than 50 Democratic lawmakers invoked the 25th Amendment to call for President Trump's removal after Trump posted a social media threat warning that 'a whole civilization will die tonight' unless Iran met his terms by a Tuesday deadline. The U.S. Treasury imposed sanctions on Nobitex, Iran's largest cryptocurrency exchange, and several of its executives, accusing the platform of helping the Iranian government evade sanctions and finance militant groups. The NY Times reported that U.S.-Iran negotiations are facing complications prolonging the process, with reporter David E. Sanger outlining key factors causing delays. Iranians inside Iran expressed fear and frustration over a potential deal, with concerns that any agreement could leave the Islamic Republic's government intact despite widespread economic devastation.

Trump claimed in a New York Post podcast interview that Iran has agreed to 'no nuclear,' stating Tehran pledged never to obtain a nuclear weapon. Trump also expressed anticipation about meeting with Iran's Supreme Leader, signaling potential direct diplomatic engagement, according to Newsmax.
A U.S. military strike in the eastern Pacific Ocean on Sunday killed three people aboard a boat accused of drug trafficking.
A separate U.S. military strike targeting a boat accused of carrying drugs in the Caribbean Sea on Monday killed two people. This follows a similar strike in the eastern Pacific the previous day.

A U.S. military strike on an alleged drug-trafficking boat in the eastern Pacific Ocean killed two men, leaving one survivor. The strike is the latest in a series of such operations conducted by the military in the region.

At least 193 people have been killed in the Trump administration's campaign of missile strikes on boats claimed to be trafficking drugs in Latin American waters. A recent U.S. strike on a boat in the Eastern Pacific killed one person while two others survived, according to SOUTHCOM.

A U.S. military strike in the eastern Pacific Ocean killed three people aboard an alleged drug-trafficking boat, the fourth such strike this week. The total death toll from the administration's campaign against alleged drug boats has now surpassed 200.
A suspect was charged with attempting to assassinate the president following a shooting at the White House Correspondents' Dinner; the charges were formally announced after the attack.

The suspect charged in the assassination attempt has been identified as Cole Allen, who has agreed to remain jailed ahead of his trial. Critics of President Trump publicly blamed his rhetoric in connection with the attack.
Cole Allen, 31, pleaded not guilty on Monday in federal court to charges related to the alleged assassination attempt against President Trump at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner.
Allen faces four total counts in the case. Monday's court proceeding was formally an arraignment, at which Allen entered not guilty pleas to all charges.

A separate incident from the Correspondents' Dinner case: U.S. Secret Service officers shot and killed a man identified as Nasire Best, 21, of Dundalk, Maryland, who opened fire at a White House security checkpoint on Saturday. CBS News reported Best had previously blocked a White House entry lane in June 2025 and had attempted to gain access to the White House the year before. A bystander was left in serious condition during the exchange of gunfire. Secret Service Director Sean Curran praised officers for their 'quick and decisive response,' and five senior law enforcement officials told NBC News that Best had a history of mental health concerns.

The White House Correspondents' Association announced Tuesday that the dinner has been rescheduled for July 24, with WHCA President Weijia Jiang making the announcement to members. President Trump announced Tuesday he will attend the rescheduled event.

Press freedom advocates warned that the rescheduled White House Correspondents' Dinner on July 24 could provide Trump a platform to attack the news media. A new article in The Atlantic by Matt Viser reported that security around the White House has been significantly tightened following the April shooting, with new perimeter measures raising questions about balancing security and public access.

timelines.title: Taylor Swift Concert Attack Plot Investigation

entries.update: An Austrian man is on trial in Austria for allegedly plotting a terrorist attack on a Taylor Swift concert in Vienna, with prosecutors alleging ties to the Islamic State.
The Austrian trial over the foiled Taylor Swift concert attack plot has entered its final day, according to Reuters.

The 21-year-old Austrian defendant was convicted and sentenced to 15 years in prison after admitting to plotting the attack on the Taylor Swift Vienna concert along with other terrorism-related offences.
The U.S. Senate blocked a Democratic-led resolution challenging Trump's military authority over Cuba, with Republican senators voting against advancing the measure.
Cuba is experiencing severe energy disruptions due to a nationwide depletion of diesel and fuel oil stocks, with the U.S.-led embargo cited as a contributing factor to the shortage.
CIA Director John Ratcliffe met with Cuban officials in Havana on Thursday to discuss economic and security issues, with both sides confirming the meeting took place.
U.S. officials are seeking to indict former Cuban leader Raúl Castro, according to U.S. officials.

A U.S. grand jury indicted Raúl Castro, now 94, along with five others on charges including murder, conspiracy to kill U.S. nationals, and destruction of aircraft related to the 1996 shootdown of two Brothers to the Rescue civilian planes that killed four Cuban Americans. Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche announced the indictment in South Florida; Castro was Cuba's armed forces minister at the time of the incident.

The USS Nimitz carrier strike group, including the destroyer USS Gridley and an air wing of F/A-18 Super Hornets and EA-18G Growlers, arrived in the Caribbean on the same day the Justice Department announced the indictment of Raúl Castro.

CIA Director Ratcliffe brought a covert operator involved in efforts to capture Nicolás Maduro to his meeting with senior Cuban officials in Havana last week. Critics accused the Trump administration of manufacturing a pretext for a potential invasion of Cuba, citing the Castro indictment and administration statements amplifying Cuba's perceived military and intelligence threat.

Cuba issued a formal warning to the United States on Saturday, asserting its 'full and exclusive sovereignty over the airspace above its territory,' in an apparent response to the federal indictment of Raúl Castro. The U.S. Treasury Department issued subpoenas to Twitch streamer Hasan Piker and CodePink cofounder Medea Benjamin as part of a federal probe into whether the two violated U.S. sanctions by traveling to Cuba, according to Fox News.
A key European airline has stopped direct flights to Cuba, with nearly a dozen airlines having cancelled or restricted flights to the country since the start of the year, according to Newsweek.
Trump, speaking at a Palm Beach forum, said the U.S. would be 'taking over' Cuba 'almost immediately,' and referenced finishing a job in Iran before turning to Cuba.

Cuba's Energy Minister Vicente de la O Levy announced on Wednesday that the country has completely exhausted its fuel oil and diesel supplies, stating 'We have absolutely no fuel (oil), and absolutely no diesel.' The minister attributed the crisis to U.S. sanctions and the blockade, which have pushed Cuba's energy system into severe collapse.

Secretary of State Rubio announced the arrest of the sister of the head of GAESA, Cuba's military business conglomerate. Rubio formally declared Cuba a national security threat to the United States, raising the prospect of military intervention, while Cuba's foreign minister accused him of spreading lies and attempting to instigate military aggression. Trump and Rubio raised the possibility of military intervention in Cuba one day after the administration announced criminal charges against former Cuban leader Raúl Castro.

Former national security adviser John Bolton warned that the Trump administration may attempt to 'kidnap or snatch' Raúl Castro, cautioning that Castro's indictment could serve as a pretext for military intervention in Cuba. The U.S. warned a peaceful agreement with Cuba is unlikely, while Havana described the situation as a 'fraudulent case' designed to justify military aggression.

Sen. Lindsey Graham declared that 'the liberation of the wonderful people of Cuba from the clutches of communism is close at hand,' backing White House threats of potential military action against the island.
The Trump administration is reportedly accelerating plans aimed at engineering the collapse of the Cuban government, according to Newsmax, though specific details of the strategy were not disclosed.
Rep. Pramila Jayapal admitted to working with Mexico on facilitating oil transfers to Cuba despite U.S. sanctions, and faced backlash following the admission.
Trump announced a three-day ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine running from May 9 to May 11, timed to coincide with Russia's Victory Day celebrations, along with a prisoner swap agreement.

Ukrainian President Zelensky stated on Sunday that he hopes White House envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will visit Kyiv for talks in the coming weeks, in an interview on CBS News's 'Face the Nation.'

Hungarian opposition leader Péter Magyar expressed readiness to meet Ukrainian President Zelenskyy, signaling a potential foreign policy shift toward Ukraine in a post-Orbán Hungary, according to Reuters.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio acknowledged on Tuesday that the prospects for a Russia-Ukraine peace deal 'don't look great,' despite extensive Trump administration efforts to end the conflict.
Tensions near the Strait of Hormuz have escalated, with one vessel seized near the UAE and taken toward Iran, and a second ship attacked and sunk off the coast of Oman.

Iran published a map asserting armed forces oversight over more than 22,000 square kilometers of the Strait of Hormuz. Despite regional tensions, OPEC+ leaders are expected to approve an increased oil output target for July, reflecting confidence in sustaining production increases.

Iran and Oman are in talks over a ship payment system related to the Strait of Hormuz, with the U.S. and Iran reported to remain far from a broader deal. Oil prices jumped as negotiations over reopening the strait reached an impasse, with disagreements persisting over Iran's uranium stockpile and proposed transit fees for the strait.

Iran and Oman have discussed establishing a toll system to charge vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz, a move that conflicts with Trump's stated opposition to transit fees on the strategic waterway. Iran's intensified closure of the strait has left sailors stranded, compounding hardships for those affected by the restrictions, according to Reuters.
Experts assess that full Iranian control over the Strait of Hormuz is unlikely, but Iran's attempts to charge vessels for passage have prompted concern within the international shipping industry.

U.S. Central Command announced it has redirected more than 100 commercial vessels as part of a naval blockade of Iranian ports in the Strait of Hormuz, describing the operation as involving more than 15,000 U.S. troops and launched in April at President Trump's direction.

Trump faces mounting pressure to reopen the Strait of Hormuz as Americans enter Memorial Day weekend with gas prices at their highest level in nearly four years, with Qatar and Pakistan acting as mediators applying pressure on Iran. British forces at Gibraltar are reported to be prepared to deploy autonomous mine-hunting equipment in the strait contingent on a peace agreement. BBC News recounted the story of Sunil Puniya, a crew member on his first sea job aboard the oil tanker Skylight, which was struck by a missile in the strait at the start of the Iran war, killing or leaving missing at least one crew member.

The U.S. and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, but key issues including Iran's nuclear stockpile, uranium enrichment, and missile program were left unresolved and have not yet been formally discussed in negotiations, according to the NY Times. The timeline for resumption of normal shipping and oil price stabilization remains uncertain.

Despite a preliminary understanding between the U.S. and Iran on Strait of Hormuz reopening, the NY Times reported that no formal agreement on resuming normal shipping has been reached, leaving the timeline for restored traffic and oil price stabilization uncertain.

Maritime experts warned that even if a deal is reached to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, moving an estimated 1,500 backlogged ships stranded for nearly three months would be a complex and lengthy process.
A tanker reported an external explosion off the coast of Oman, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO), which confirmed the crew is safe.
President Trump threatened serious repercussions if Iran and Oman proceeded with a deal to open the Strait of Hormuz, before adding 'They'll be fine,' according to the NY Times.

The U.S. Treasury Department sanctioned Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA), a newly formed Iranian government agency, describing it as an IRGC attempt to control and monetize passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

The U.S. and Iran have entered an economic standoff in the Strait of Hormuz, with an American blockade and Iranian control of the strait creating a stalemate as both sides attempt economic strangulation through naval presence, according to the NY Times.

National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett predicted on ABC's 'This Week' that oil shipments will resume through the Strait of Hormuz within 'a month or two,' noting there is already 'a lot more traffic' passing through the strait. U.S. Central Command has quietly guided approximately 70 commercial ships through the Strait of Hormuz over a three-week period, according to a U.S. official.

Iran's state-affiliated Tasnim News Agency announced that Tehran is halting indirect message exchanges with the United States and may move to close the Strait of Hormuz, citing U.S. ceasefire violations as justification.

Many large oil tankers remain stranded in the Strait of Hormuz, with uncertainty over whether they will return to Middle East routes in significant numbers once they are able to leave, according to the Wall Street Journal.

Approximately 20,000 seafarers remain trapped in the Iran war zone, reporting stress and exhaustion after months of being blocked by the Strait of Hormuz blockade, according to BBC News. U.S. Central Command announced that the U.S. military disabled the engine of a ship attempting to break through the blockade of Iran's ports.

WTI crude futures rose for a third consecutive day, gaining nearly 10% over three sessions, as hopes for a quick peace deal faded, according to the Wall Street Journal. Secretary of State Rubio told lawmakers that the war on Iran is over, amid reports of recent strikes hitting Iran, Kuwait, and Bahrain.
More oil shipments are passing through the Strait of Hormuz, according to Reuters, leaving energy traders uncertain about supply flows through the waterway.

timelines.title: Raúl Castro Indictment for 1996 Plane Downing

entries.update: The DOJ is pushing to indict former Cuban President Raúl Castro in connection with Cuba's 1996 downing of civilian planes, according to U.S. officials familiar with the matter.

A Florida-seated U.S. grand jury formally indicted former Cuban leader Raúl Castro on charges including murder and conspiracy to kill U.S. nationals, in connection with Cuba's 1996 shootdown of two Brothers to the Rescue civilian planes. The indictment was announced Wednesday.

A Florida grand jury indicted Raúl Castro and five others in connection with the 1996 shootdown. China criticized the U.S. for what it called 'threats' against Cuba following the indictment. Russia expressed full solidarity with Cuba and pledged active support amid escalating U.S. pressure, which also included Secretary of State Rubio messaging that appeared to encourage Cubans to overthrow their government. The U.S. Supreme Court issued an 8-1 ruling by Justice Clarence Thomas limiting lawsuits over property seized by Cuba. Senator Rubio stated the likelihood of a negotiated agreement with Cuba is low. The indictment is circulating among Cubans amid widespread blackouts, with many expressing hope it could improve their living conditions.

Luis González-Pardo, a Cuban pilot living in Florida, was identified as one of the named defendants in the federal indictment alongside Raúl Castro. Cuban officials publicly rallied in support of Castro following his indictment on murder charges.
Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum publicly protested the U.S. indictment of Raúl Castro at a Friday press conference, arguing the 1996 incident occurred too long ago to warrant charges.

Luis Raúl González-Pardo Rodríguez, the Cuban pilot named as a defendant in the Raúl Castro indictment, was sentenced for providing false information to U.S. immigration authorities during his application for permanent residency.

The DOJ formally filed its intent to seek the death penalty for the suspect accused of shooting and killing two Israeli Embassy staffers outside a Jewish museum in Washington, D.C. The filing was submitted to a federal judge on a Friday and is associated with U.S. Attorney for D.C. Jeanine Pirro.

A judge declared a mistrial in Harvey Weinstein's third Manhattan sex crimes rape retrial after the jury deadlocked and was unable to reach a verdict. The charges were brought by accuser Jessica Mann.
The WHO declared the Ebola outbreak affecting DR Congo and Uganda a global public health emergency, with approximately 80 deaths reported across both countries.

An Air France flight bound for Detroit was diverted to Canada after a passenger from the DRC boarded 'in error,' prompting Ebola-related concerns. The Department of Homeland Security announced new arrival restrictions for travelers from the DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan. Enhanced Ebola screening is now required at Washington Dulles International Airport for U.S.-bound travelers from affected African countries. The WHO reported the death toll in Congo has risen to 134, with the WHO chief expressing alarm at the outbreak's rapid spread and scale. India postponed an Africa summit due to the virus spreading into M23-controlled territory in eastern DRC, where armed conflict has complicated containment efforts. Russia expressed solidarity with Cuba and promised active support amid escalating U.S. pressure on the Castro regime.

The U.S. imposed new travel restrictions formally barring entry to non-U.S. passport holders who have visited the DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan within the past three weeks. Trump administration officials also issued quarantine orders regarding Ebola and hantavirus that public health experts described as going beyond what is necessary, with experts expressing being stunned by the strictness of the measures.

UK scientists are developing a new vaccine targeting the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, which kills approximately one third of those infected and has no proven vaccine, with the candidate potentially ready within months. Former CDC epidemiologist Dr. Neil Vora warned the outbreak will 'get worse before it gets better,' citing his experience during the 2019 DRC outbreak. NBC News reported the outbreak is being further hampered by misinformation, strained resources, and armed conflict, with healthcare workers among the first reported cases.

The Trump administration expanded its pause on U.S. visa processing to additional embassies beyond the initial suspension at Uganda, South Sudan, and DRC posts. Suspected Ebola cases in the DRC have grown to nearly 750, prompting health authorities to intensify measures along the DRC–Uganda border, disrupting daily life in the region. BBC News gathered perspectives from survivors and experts of the West Africa outbreak a decade ago, highlighting lessons on speed, funding, and compassion.

Three Red Cross workers died from Ebola in DR Congo. Uganda confirmed three new cases, bringing its total to five, including a driver who transported the country's first confirmed patient and a health worker. The CDC expanded enhanced Ebola screening to Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, the world's busiest, targeting passengers arriving from Congo, Uganda, and South Sudan. The Trump administration further tightened travel restrictions to include lawful permanent residents (green card holders) who have been in the DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan within the past 21 days, with the update issued by the Department of Health and Human Services. U.S. citizens and permanent residents departing Ebola-affected countries are now required to enter the U.S. through one of three designated airports. DR Congo stated it would not alter its World Cup preparations despite a U.S. warning to its soccer team to isolate due to Ebola concerns.

The WHO declared a global public health emergency over the Ebola resurgence in central Africa, citing the rare Bundibugyo strain cases in Congo and Uganda. Eighteen individuals with suspected Ebola cases fled a treatment facility and remain unaccounted for after a second treatment tent was set on fire amid growing local anger over burial practices conflicting with traditional customs. U.S. officials expanded Ebola airport screening to a third location, directing passengers from high-risk countries to Atlanta, Houston, or Washington D.C., and increased the number of designated high-risk African countries from three to ten.

Uganda confirmed three additional Ebola cases as DR Congo's neighboring countries intensified monitoring with Covid-style cross-border restrictions. A senior Médecins Sans Frontières official, Kate White, warned of being 'extremely concerned about the inability to get resources' to the affected region. NPR reported the outbreak is spreading amid distrust and armed conflict, with infections threatening a total of 10 countries across the region.

The WHO chief reported more than 900 suspected Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Public health experts stated that U.S. withdrawal from global health programs under the Trump administration is hampering the outbreak response, describing it as the first major outbreak since those programs were dismantled. Young men stormed a hospital in Congo treating Ebola patients, demanding the bodies of their relatives. A former Trump COVID adviser stated the U.S. is equipped to handle an Ebola outbreak but noted the CDC and FDA currently lack confirmed leaders.
The NY Times reported that the Congo outbreak is only now beginning to see a coordinated response take shape, after authorities were caught unprepared by the virus's rapid spread in its early months.

WHO Director-General Tedros stated suspected Ebola deaths have reached 220, warning the epidemic is 'outpacing' responders and that delays in case detection have left officials 'playing catch-up.' Uganda reported two new cases, bringing its total to seven. Police fired shots into the air to disperse angry crowds at a treatment centre in Congo as unrest over body recovery continued, with attacks on health facilities causing additional patients to flee and further hampering the response.

Canada imposed a travel ban related to the Ebola outbreak, while the Bahamas announced plans to increase screening measures, according to Reuters. Communities in western Uganda, approximately 200 miles from the outbreak epicenter, are reporting significant economic anxiety as the crisis threatens the tourism industry sustaining livelihoods in areas like Katunguru near Queen Elizabeth National Park.

The DRC Ebola outbreak has surpassed 1,000 confirmed or suspected cases, and the U.S. announced plans for a quarantine site and is seeking volunteers in response. WHO Director-General Tedros warned of a 'catastrophic collision' of Ebola and armed conflict in the DRC, stating that halting transmission depends entirely on humanitarian access. A doctor who died treating Ebola patients in the DRC has been buried. Health officials are also contending with unfamiliar species of Ebola and hantavirus that differ significantly from strains identified decades ago, raising new questions about response strategies, according to the NY Times.

The Trump administration announced plans to quarantine Americans exposed to Ebola at a new treatment facility being constructed in Kenya, with public health service officers preparing for rapid deployment to staff the site. The Department of Homeland Security confirmed that JFK International Airport has been added to the limited list of U.S. entry points designated for travelers from Ebola-affected nations, joining existing screening sites at major U.S. cities.

Doctors at the Ebola outbreak epicenter in eastern DRC told ABC News the virus remains 'out of control' and is still spreading at an alarming rate. The U.S., Mexico, and Canada announced Ebola-related travel measures ahead of the FIFA World Cup, which the three nations are jointly hosting beginning in June.

A Kenyan court on Friday temporarily blocked the U.S. plan to construct an Ebola quarantine facility for Americans in Kenya. The WHO reported 906 suspected cases and 223 suspected deaths from the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola. NPR reported that community members in affected areas are attacking Ebola clinics and distrusting medical workers, with traditional burial practices posing additional transmission risks.

WHO Director-General Tedros announced that five people infected with the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola have recovered in eastern Congo, making the announcement during a visit to Bunia. Africa CDC reported 263 confirmed cases and 43 deaths across Congo and Uganda. Brazil is monitoring two patients for possible Ebola infection, which if confirmed would be the first cases outside Africa since the current outbreak began.

Aid workers in Uganda report that foreign aid cuts are hampering preparations for a potential spillover of the Ebola outbreak from the DRC. The NY Times reported on conditions inside an Ebola ward while highlighting obstacles facing Trump's $1.8 billion fund designated for related health efforts. Newsweek noted that the 2025 summer travel season is coinciding with elevated infectious disease concerns, including Ebola, mpox, and flesh-eating parasites.

Suspected Ebola cases have surpassed 1,100 globally as Brazil launched a formal investigation into two patients in Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo hospitals exhibiting Ebola-like symptoms. Moderna and other groups received $60 million in funding to develop an Ebola vaccine, according to Reuters.

The International Rescue Committee warned that the Ebola outbreak in the DRC is 'likely far worse' than official figures suggest. Two people were killed in Kenya during a protest against the U.S. plan to establish an Ebola quarantine site, according to a protest organiser and a source cited by Reuters. BBC News reported that health workers are responding to the Bundibugyo strain for which no approved targeted treatments currently exist.

A Kenyan court issued a ruling further delaying the Trump administration's proposed 50-bed Ebola quarantine facility for Americans exposed to the virus, a plan that has already sparked violent protests and prompted Kenya's president to publicly defend the center. The IRC indicated the current outbreak may have been spreading undetected since as early as January, while NPR highlighted the gap between the intensive care Ebola requires and the limited healthcare resources available in the DRC. A chronic lack of diagnostic testing infrastructure in Congo is hampering containment efforts, according to the NY Times.
Demonstrators in Nairobi, Kenya carried an 'Ebola coffin' in protest against the proposed U.S. quarantine facility, opposing its establishment in the country.

Secretary of State Rubio rejected accusations that Trump administration funding cuts contributed to the Ebola outbreak, as health workers blamed U.S. cutbacks for enabling the crisis. The mayor of La Línea de la Concepción, Spain, banned a planned friendly football match between DR Congo and Chile over Ebola health concerns.
U.S. equipment and experts arrived at the Kenya Ebola facility despite an existing court order and ongoing protests against the installation, according to Reuters.
Cristian Fajardo Mondragon, 17, was named as a suspect in an Austin shooting spree involving 12 attacks over approximately 28 hours. Three juveniles were arrested in connection with the incident.
Three adults were killed in a shooting at the Islamic Center of San Diego on Monday, with both suspects also dead. Authorities are investigating the attack as a suspected hate crime.
Writings attributed to the suspects contain extremist neo-Nazi ideology and apparent incel-related influences, according to authorities.

A memorial drew thousands of mourners honoring the three victims, who were remembered as heroes. Authorities revealed that only 7 officers were assigned to the area at the time of the attack. In 2025, police had seized approximately a dozen firearms from the home of suspect Caleb Vazquez after his father surrendered them following reports about Vazquez's obsession with mass shooters and Nazism. Vazquez's family issued a public statement saying his exposure to hateful and extremist online content contributed to his radicalization, and apologized for his alleged actions.

Online associates of suspect Caleb Vazquez told the New York Post that he allegedly joked about killing Muslim and Jewish people in a radical-right group chat and was obsessed with a 'based racist' Dutch cartoon character.
More than 25,000 Muslim Americans gathered at the annual ICNA conference following the San Diego shooting, where speakers encouraged turning grief into civic and political activism.

At least 131 people have died in the Congo Ebola outbreak, prompting the WHO to express concern over its speed and scale. An American medical missionary who tested positive for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo is being transported to Germany for treatment.

A Kenyan court suspended the U.S. plan to establish an Ebola quarantine facility in Kenya, which the Trump administration had confirmed it was working to set up for Americans exposed to or infected with Ebola. WHO Director-General traveled to Kinshasa to personally assess the outbreak response, amid ongoing challenges including local distrust and insecurity.

timelines.title: Iran Nuclear Deal Negotiations and Regional Tensions

entries.update: Trump declared Abraham Accords participation 'mandatory' for any country seeking involvement in a prospective Iran deal. Trump publicly attacked critics of the emerging agreement, calling Democratic opponents, RINOs, and others 'weak and ineffective fools.' The Wall Street Journal editorial board warned the administration against offering Iran an 'economic bailout,' cautioning that ceasefire terms 'may deliver a strategic setback' for the U.S. Israeli opposition leader Yair Lapid called the emerging framework 'a disaster.'

Fresh U.S. airstrikes on southern Iran on Monday cast doubt on the progress of ongoing negotiations, even as a fierce public relations battle over a potential deal continued. Trump's social media posts over the weekend created confusion regarding the status of the Iran negotiations, according to NBC News. Trump convened a Cabinet meeting Wednesday amid the ongoing negotiations and mounting criticism of the emerging deal. The EU launched a fertiliser plan in response to disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz stemming from the Iran war, citing growing food security concerns in Europe.

President Trump called for more countries to recognize Israel as a condition for ending the war with Iran, proposing an expansion of the Abraham Accords. Analysts cited by the NY Times described the likelihood of such an expansion as close to zero, with the proposal being met with bewilderment across the Middle East.

President Trump made edits to a possible U.S.-Iran agreement, with requested changes related to the Strait of Hormuz and the removal of highly enriched uranium, according to CBS News and other U.S. media reports. French President Macron called on Middle Eastern leaders to help the U.S. and Iran seize a diplomatic opening, stating he met with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Omani Sultan Haitham bin Tariq, and Emirati leaders as part of these efforts. The United States proposed a 'roadmap' for de-escalation in Lebanon, according to a U.S. official. Israel's historic ground incursion into Lebanon is reported to be complicating ongoing Iran deal efforts. Trump's consideration of an Iran deal is sparking an intra-Republican debate, with Senate Armed Services Committee Chair Roger Wicker expected to lead opposition from defense hawks.

Iran suspended peace talks with the United States specifically to protest Israel's expanding offensive in Lebanon, with Iranian officials demanding a ceasefire on all fronts before negotiations could resume. President Trump told NBC News he had not been informed of the suspension.
